project.title: Circuit basics — simulate, build, and measure
project.objective: Understand voltage division, load effects, and RC timing by comparing predictions, ideal simulations, and a separate low-voltage breadboard build.
iteration_exit_criteria: Voltage-divider and loading predictions are checked against physical readings.
An RC charge/discharge curve is measured and its approximate time constant explained.
Predicted, simulated, and measured evidence remain distinguishable.
Any unavailable physical work is recorded as pending or blocked, not passed by simulation alone.
out_of_scope_for_iteration: Automatic GitHub writes or automatic completion of bench milestones

nodes.title: Prepare the bench and prediction log
nodes.summary: Gather parts, identify breadboard connections and meter sockets, and open the first lesson. No physical measurements have been recorded yet.
acceptance_criteria: A separate approximately 3 V breadboard setup is available, or missing parts are explicitly listed.
Meter voltage versus resistance modes and capacitor polarity are understood.
Predicted, simulated and measured values have separate headings in the notes.
outputs: Bench setup and parts checklist; open questions

nodes.title: Voltage, resistance, and a divider
nodes.summary: Explain why two equal series resistors produce half the supply voltage, then check a real build.
acceptance_criteria: Prediction recorded before revealing ideal answers.
Baseline and at least one variation checked in simulation.
Physical circuit built and readings recorded with probe nodes, units, and power state.
Differences between prediction, simulation, and measurement explained or left as specific open questions.
outputs: LESSON-001 field notes with prediction, simulation, and measured evidence

nodes.title: A measurement or load changes the circuit

acceptance_criteria: Prediction recorded before revealing ideal answers.

nodes.title: Review and apply the lessons
nodes.summary: Explain reference nodes, loading, and RC timing in your own words. Relate them to future microphone tracing without assigning unverified microphone component values or functions.
acceptance_criteria: All three lessons have physical evidence or a clearly recorded blocker.
Ground reference, loading, and time constant can each be explained using a measured example.
Remaining questions and a next exercise are recorded; incomplete physical work is not marked complete.
outputs: Tutorial summary and next learning goal
